raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary
The default OpenCV video decoder walks every source frame up to the last sampled index via sequential `cap.grab()`. Uniform sampling always includes that last index, so decode CPU tracks container frame count rather than the small number of returned frames. A long, highly compressible video stays under the download-size cap and can occupy a media worker for the full walk. This adds `VLLM_MAX_VIDEO_DECODE_FRAMES` (default 36000, `0` disables) and rejects over-budget walks before either OpenCV grab loop starts.

## Changes
- `vllm/envs.py`: add `VLLM_MAX_VIDEO_DECODE_FRAMES`.
- `vllm/multimodal/video_decoders/base.py`: reject walks above the cap.
- `vllm/multimodal/video_decoders/opencv.py`: enforce the cap in `read_frames` (covers recovery and non-recovery paths).
- `docs/usage/security.md`: document the new decode-size guard.
- Tests for under-limit, over-limit (both recovery modes), disable-with-0, and the `VideoMediaIO` entry point.

## Codepath coverage
- Chat / messages / responses / batch / `/invocations` / gRPC / offline `LLM.generate` all reach `VideoMediaIO` → OpenCV `read_frames`: covered.
- `video/jpeg` base64 and TorchCodec / PyNvVideoCodec / DeepStream do not use this grab loop: N/A.
- GLM-5.1 seek-based `read_frames` override does not use the sequential grab loop unless `frame_recovery=True` (then it calls the shared `read_frames`): covered on that recovery path.

## Duplicate-work check
Searched open, draft, and recently merged PRs for OpenCV `read_frames`, `cap.grab`, video decode frame/duration limits, and `video_decoders/opencv`. #55582 speeds GLM sampler index selection; #46836 adds an encoded-file size guard; #51969 clamps request `num_frames` for `video/jpeg`. None of those bound the OpenCV sequential grab loop.

## Tests
- `test_opencv_decode_frame_limit_respected`
- `test_opencv_decode_frame_limit_rejected` (frame_recovery false/true)
- `test_opencv_decode_frame_limit_disabled`
- `test_video_media_io_decode_frame_limit_rejected`

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/multimodal/test_video.py::test_opencv_decode_frame_limit_respected \
  tests/multimodal/test_video.py::test_opencv_decode_frame_limit_rejected \
  tests/multimodal/test_video.py::test_opencv_decode_frame_limit_disabled \
  tests/multimodal/media/test_video.py::test_video_media_io_decode_frame_limit_rejected -v
```

5 passed.

`.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files` on the changed files passed.

## AI assistance
This PR was developed with AI assistance.

Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

Rebased onto upstream main, preserving the original fix and current surrounding behavior. The duplicate audit found no complete merged or open replacement for this PR’s remaining control.

 | `VLLM_MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS` | `178956970` (~179M pixels) | Maximum decoded image size in pixels. Images exceeding this are rejected before raster memory is allocated. Default matches PIL's built-in 2x decompression-bomb threshold (~680 MB for RGB). |
 | `VLLM_MAX_MEDIA_REQUEST_DECODE_BYTES` | `715827880` (~683 MiB) | Maximum aggregate decoded image, video-frame, and audio bytes in one request. Images are charged at four bytes per pixel before decoding; audio is limited before decoding; video files are charged after frame extraction. |
+| `VLLM_MAX_VIDEO_DECODE_FRAMES` | `36000` | Maximum source frames the default OpenCV video decoder may walk. Uniform sampling still includes the last frame, so sequential `cap.grab()` work tracks the container frame count, not the number of returned frames. Videos that would walk more frames are rejected before decode. Default is 10 minutes at 60 FPS. |
 | `VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_CLIP_FILESIZE_MB` | `25` | Maximum compressed filesize in MB for a single audio file. Enforced on all audio inputs (multimodal chat URLs, speech-to-text uploads, data: URLs, and local file paths) before decoding begins. |
 | `VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_DECODE_DURATION_S` | `600` | Maximum decoded audio duration in seconds. Prevents compressed audio from expanding into gigabytes of float32 PCM. |
 | `VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_DECODE_BYTES` | `268435456` (256 MiB) | Maximum float32 PCM bytes that audio decoding may allocate. Guards against sample-rate forgery where an inflated header sample rate bypasses the duration guard while the actual frame count causes a multi-GiB allocation. |
